pairs: Confirmatum est igitur regnum in manu Salomonis,
And so the kingdom was confirmed in the hand of Solomon,
et affinitate conjunctus est Pharaoni regi Ægypti:
and he was joined with Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, by affinity.
and he led her into the city of David,
until he completed building his own house,
and the house of the Lord,
and the wall of Jerusalem all around.
But still the people immolated in the high places.
non enim ædificatum erat templum nomini Domini usque in diem illum.
For no temple had been built to the name of the Lord, even to that day.
ambulans in præceptis David patris sui,
walking in the precepts of David, his father,
except that he immolated in the high places,
And so, he went away to Gibeon,
ut immolaret ibi: illud quippe erat excelsum maximum:
so that he might immolate there; for that was the greatest high place.
mille hostias in holocaustum obtulit Salomon super altare illud in Gabaon.
Solomon offered upon that altar, at Gibeon, one thousand victims as holocausts.
Apparuit autem Dominus Salomoni per somnium nocte,
Then the Lord appeared to Solomon, through a dream in the night, saying,
dicens: Postula quod vis ut dem tibi.
“Request whatever you wish, so that I may give it to you.”
Tu fecisti cum servo tuo David patre meo misericordiam magnam,
“You have shown great mercy to your servant David,
sicut ambulavit in conspectu tuo in veritate
because he walked in your sight in truth and justice,
and with an upright heart before you.
And you have kept your great mercy for him,
et dedisti ei filium sedentem super thronum ejus,
and you have given him a son sitting upon his throne,
just as it is this day.
tu regnare fecisti servum tuum pro David patre meo:
you have caused your servant to reign in place of David,
my father. But I am a small child,
et ignorans egressum et introitum meum.
and I am ignorant of my entrance and departure.
Et servus tuus in medio est populi quem elegisti,
And your servant is in the midst of the people that you have chosen,
qui numerari et supputari non potest præ multitudine.
who are not able to be numbered or counted because of their multitude.
Dabis ergo servo tuo cor docile,
Therefore, give to your servant a teachable heart,
so that he may be able to judge your people,
et discernere inter bonum et malum.
and to discern between good and evil.
Quis enim poterit judicare populum istum,
For who will be able to judge this people,
your people, who are so many?”
And the word was pleasing before the Lord,
that Solomon had requested this kind of thing.
And the Lord said to Solomon:
et non petisti tibi dies multos,
and you have not asked for many days
nor for the lives of your enemies,
sed postulasti tibi sapientiam ad discernendum judicium:
but instead you have requested for yourself wisdom in order to discern judgment:
ecce feci tibi secundum sermones tuos,
I have done for you according to your words,
and I have given you a wise and understanding heart,
in tantum ut nullus ante te similis tui fuerit,
so much so that there has been no one like you before you,
nor anyone who will rise up after you.
Sed et hæc quæ non postulasti,
But also the things for which you did not ask,
ut nemo fuerit similis tui in regibus cunctis retro diebus.
so that no one has been like you among the kings in the all days before.
Si autem ambulaveris in viis meis,
And if you will walk in my ways,
et custodieris præcepta mea et mandata mea,
and keep my precepts and my commandments,
and he understood that it was a dream.
And when he had arrived in Jerusalem,
he stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord,
and made victims of peace offerings,
et grande convivium universis famulis suis.
and he held a great feast for all his servants.
Tunc venerunt duæ mulieres meretrices ad regem,
Then two women harlots went to the king,
I and this woman were living in one house,
et mulier hæc habitabamus in domo una,
et peperi apud eam in cubiculo.
Tertia autem die postquam ego peperi,
on the third day after I gave birth,
with no other person with us in the house,
Mortuus est autem filius mulieris hujus nocte:
Then this woman’s son died in the night.
For while sleeping, she smothered him.
And rising up in the silent depths of the night,
tulit filium meum de latere meo,
she took my son from my side,
and she set him in her bosom.
Then she placed her dead son in my bosom.
Cumque surrexissem mane ut darem lac filio meo,
And when I had arisen in the morning, so that I might give milk to my son,
But gazing upon him more diligently in the light of day,
deprehendi non esse meum quem genueram.
I realized that he was not mine, whom I had born.”
“It is not such as you say.
“You are lying. For my son lives,
Atque in hunc modum contendebant coram rege.
And in this manner, they were contending before the king.
And when they had brought a sword before the king,
inquit, infantem vivum in duas partes,
“Divide the living infant in two parts,
et date dimidiam partem uni, et dimidiam partem alteri.
and give a half part to the one and a half part to the other.”
ad regem (commota sunt quippe viscera ejus super filio suo):
said to the king, for her heart was moved concerning her son,
give the living infant to her,
To the contrary, the other said,
“Let it be neither for me, nor for you,
“Give the living infant to this woman,
Audivit itaque omnis Israël judicium quod judicasset rex,
Then all of Israel heard about the judgment that the king had judged,
videntes sapientiam Dei esse in eo ad faciendum judicium.
seeing that the wisdom of God was in him to accomplish judgment.
